children: Grades were mixed on Friday, dealers said, as a hurricane barreled toward the coast and producers shut in some offshore production, while the domestic rig count climbed to its highest in more than a year.

US producers in the Gulf of Mexico shut in about 1.5 million barrels per day of oil production and 1.3 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas, an increase from the prior day, as Hurricane Isaias churned toward the coast ahead of an expected landfall along the Florida Panhandle later on Friday.
The shut-ins represent nearly 72% and 59% of US oil and natural gas production in the Gulf, respectively, according to the Marine Minerals Administration.
Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by six to 462 this week, their highest since May 2025, while gas rigs fell by one to 132, their lowest since mid-September, and other miscellaneous rigs held at nine.
In the Permian Shale in West Texas and eastern New Mexico, the rig count rose by four to 274, the highest since June 2025.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace after what Trump described as a "highly successful" discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
